title: Gideon and the Deadline
premise: Zephyrine Underhill, a freelance interpreter who has built a career on being forgettable, is attached to a fragile peace delegation in the Baltic city of Velsund. A burner phone left in her coat pocket rings with the voice of her presumed-dead brother, who is alive, compromised, and holding evidence that the delegation's brokered ceasefire is a laundering scheme for war crimes. To save him, she must extract the evidence from the delegation's own security chief—the man she has quietly fallen for—before a dawn extraction flight becomes either their escape or their grave. She trades the evidence for his life at the airstrip, burns her own anonymity in the process, and ends the book testifying under her real name, choosing truth over the invisibility that once kept her safe.
about_author: Theo Thackeray is the pen name of a former NGO field coordinator who spent a decade in negotiation rooms across Eastern Europe before turning to fiction. He writes from a farmhouse in Wales, where he claims the best plot twists arrive during power cuts.

chapters.title: The Interpreter's Rule
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. She arrives in Velsund, establishing her craft: translate exactly, reveal nothing, be no one. A colleague jokes she could vanish mid-sentence and no one would notice. Emotional beat: the comfort and quiet loneliness of invisibility.

chapters.title: Delegation of the Doomed
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. First plenary session; she reads the room's hostility through tone and hesitation, sensing the ceasefire will fail. She notices security chief Marek Voss watching her too closely. Emotional beat: professional unease sharpening into awareness.

chapters.title: A Coat Not Hers
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. After a reception, she finds a cheap burner phone in her coat pocket. No contacts, one saved number. She tells no one. Emotional beat: a cold prickle of being seen for the first time in years.

chapters.title: The Voice
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. The phone rings at 3 a.m.: her brother Tomas, dead for two years by all official record. He says only, 'You're already being followed. Trust the phone, not the delegation.' Emotional beat: grief detonating into disbelief.

chapters.title: Marek
chapters.summary: Marek Voss's POV. He runs the delegation's security, reports to a handler he despises, and has flagged Zephyrine's name on an old watchlist. He chooses not to report her—yet. Emotional beat: duty at war with a growing, unwelcome protectiveness.

chapters.title: Watching the Watchers
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. She tests her surveillance: same grey sedan, same café mirror glances. Using interpreter's tricks, she confirms she's being followed by two separate teams. Emotional beat: fear transmuted into cold competence.

chapters.title: Terms of Silence
chapters.summary: Zephyrine and Tomas's POV, alternating calls. Tomas explains he faked his death after discovering the ceasefire conceals a sanctions-evasion network; the proof is inside the delegation. Emotional beat: sibling intimacy rekindled under impossible conditions.

chapters.title: The Broker
chapters.summary: Delegation mediator Ilse Brandt's POV. She privately meets a shadowy fixer, Korzen, who guarantees the deal's 'success' in exchange for a list of names. She agrees, telling herself it's diplomacy. Emotional beat: rationalization curdling into complicity.

chapters.title: Coffee, Carefully
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Marek approaches her over coffee, probing without accusing. Their verbal sparring doubles as attraction; both are fluent in what isn't said. Emotional beat: connection that feels like danger.

chapters.title: The Watchlist
chapters.summary: Marek's POV. His handler orders him to surveil Zephyrine fully. He stalls, falsifying a report. Emotional beat: first small treason, justified as instinct.

chapters.title: Translation as Weapon
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. During a tense session, she subtly mistranslates a phrase to buy Tomas time, realizing her skill can be a blade. Emotional beat: exhilaration shadowed by the line she just crossed.

chapters.title: What Tomas Found
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Flashback: two years ago, he copied a ledger implicating Korzen's network and delegation insiders, then staged his death when they came for him. Emotional beat: guilt—he dragged her in by using the phone.

chapters.title: The Grey Sedan
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. She's nearly grabbed in a parking garage; Marek intervenes, claiming she's 'his asset' to the attackers. Emotional beat: rescue that binds them, and the terrifying question of what he now knows.

chapters.title: Interrogation by Candlelight
chapters.summary: Marek's POV. He confronts Zephyrine in a safe flat. She lies brilliantly; he lets her, revealing only that he didn't report the garage incident. Emotional beat: mutual recognition of two people keeping secrets.

chapters.title: Ilse's List
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Korzen demands the names; Ilse realizes the list includes people she's promised to protect. She begins quietly hedging, copying documents. Emotional beat: a decent woman sliding toward the edge.

chapters.title: Burner Protocol
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Tomas gives her the extraction plan: a dawn flight from a private airstrip in six days; the evidence must be in hand by then. Emotional beat: a ticking clock made flesh.

chapters.title: The Ledger's Shadow
chapters.summary: Zephyrine and Marek's POV. Independently, both trace the network's money to a Velsund shipping firm. Their investigations collide in the firm's lobby. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance.

chapters.title: Confession at the Harbor
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. She tells Marek everything—Tomas, the phone, the ledger. He doesn't arrest her. Emotional beat: love admitted in the grammar of trust, not words.

chapters.title: Marek's Handler
chapters.summary: Marek's POV. His handler reveals he knows about the harbor meeting and offers him a promotion for delivering Zephyrine. Emotional beat: the trap closing from inside his own chain of command.

chapters.title: Ilse Defects, Almost
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Zephyrine approaches her through a translation session; Ilse denies everything but leaves a document where Zephyrine will find it. Emotional beat: cowardice and conscience sharing one body.

chapters.title: The Shipping Office
chapters.summary: Zephyrine and Marek's POV. Night break-in at the shipping firm; they find the ledger's matching copy and a manifest of 'passengers'—people, not cargo. Emotional beat: horror converting the mission from personal to moral.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Corridor
chapters.summary: Marek's deputy, bought by Korzen, photographs them leaving the office. Marek's stalling is over. Emotional beat: the net tightening.

chapters.title: House of Mirrors
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. The delegation announces an early 'success' ceremony—two days ahead of schedule, before the extraction flight. Korzen is engineering the timeline. Emotional beat: the clock shortened, panic disciplined into planning.

chapters.title: What Marek Owes
chapters.summary: Marek's POV. Backstory: years ago his silence let a village burn; the ledger names him as a witness who did nothing. Emotional beat: shame as the engine of his choice to finally act.

chapters.title: The Ceremony
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. She interprets the signing while passing a microSD card through a handshake, watched by three people who may or may not be Korzen's. Emotional beat: high-wire tension in plain sight.

chapters.title: Ilse's Price
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Korzen confronts her about the copied documents; she trades her silence for a seat on the extraction flight. Emotional beat: survival dressed up as redemption.

chapters.title: The Deputy's Move
chapters.summary: Deputy Rask's POV. He sells Marek out fully, tipping Korzen about the airstrip. Emotional beat: banality of treachery—a man doing evil for a flat and a pension.

chapters.title: Tomas on the Line
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Final call: he's been captured; Korzen offers a trade—the ledger for Tomas, at the airstrip, tonight, not dawn. Emotional beat: Zephyrine's brother used as bait against her conscience.

chapters.title: Two Clocks
chapters.summary: Zephyrine and Marek's POV. They realize the trade and the extraction can't both be real; one is a trap. Marek proposes splitting the evidence: half to the trade, half to journalists. Emotional beat: love against duty, argued and chosen.

chapters.title: The Split
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. They divide the ledger; she keeps the names, he takes the financials to a waiting reporter. A quiet, almost tender scene before the storm. Emotional beat: vows made without ceremony.

chapters.title: Rask's Ambush
chapters.summary: Marek's POV. Rask tries to stop them at the safe flat; Marek subdues him but takes a bullet graze. Emotional beat: violence arriving at last, and the cost made physical.

chapters.title: Night Drive to Velsund Airfield
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. The drive through rain and roadblocks, Marek bleeding, the phone silent. Emotional beat: dread and devotion in the same breath.

chapters.title: The Trade
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. On the tarmac, she hands over the ledger chip for Tomas. Korzen's men release her brother—and then Korzen reveals the flight has been reported and will be seized on arrival. Emotional beat: victory inverted.

chapters.title: Korzen's Mistake
chapters.summary: Marek's POV. Korzen gloats that Marek's handler ordered the seizure—but Marek recorded the handler's voice on the burner, implicating the delegation itself. Emotional beat: the trapdoor swinging under the trapper.

chapters.title: Runway Fire
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Chaos: Ilse, arriving for her seat, broadcasts Korzen's arrival over the airfield frequency, bringing customs police instead of Korzen's men. Gunfire, fog, the plane's engines. Emotional beat: the invisible woman becoming the most visible person on the field.

chapters.title: What Zephyrine Trades
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Cornered, she offers the only thing Korzen truly fears: her testimony as the interpreter who heard every session, in exchange for letting the plane leave. Korzen, facing exposure, accepts. Emotional beat: trading the secret worth killing for—her own silence.

chapters.title: Dawn
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The plane lifts with Zephyrine, Marek, Tomas, and Ilse as Korzen is detained on the tarmac. The burner phone rings one last time; she lets it ring out. Emotional beat: exhaustion, relief, and the death of her old life.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV, months later. In a tribunal chamber in The Hague, she gives her name in full for the record. Marek waits outside, no longer her security chief, just a man who stayed. Emotional beat: justice inside the law at last, chosen freely.

chapters.title: The Names We Keep
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. He and Zephyrine visit their mother's grave together, his death officially reversed. Some of the ledger's names were never prosecuted; the siblings accept the imperfect arithmetic. Emotional beat: grief settled, loyalty redefined around truth.

chapters.title: A New Assignment
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. An offer arrives: interpret for the war crimes prosecutions she made possible. She accepts—visible, named, on the record. Final line echoes chapter one: she could vanish anytime; she chooses not to. Emotional beat: love against duty resolved into love as duty.
